'''Angela K. Wilson''' is an American scientist and former (2022) [[Presidents of the American Chemical Society|President of the]] [[American Chemical Society]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Wang |first=Linda |title=Angela K. Wilson is 2021 ACS president-elect{{!}} Chemical & Engineering News |url=https://cen.acs.org/acs-news/elections/Angela-K-Wilson-is-2021-ACS-president-elect/98/web/2020/10 |access-date=2020-10-28 |website=cen.acs.org}}</ref>  She currently serves as the Vice President for Research at [[Texas A&M University]] and the VPR Research Chair, with an appointment in the Department of Chemistry.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Read |first=5 Min |date=2025-12-17 |title=Texas A&M University names Dr. Angela Wilson as vice president for research |url=https://stories.tamu.edu/news/2025/12/17/texas-am-university-names-dr-angela-wilson-as-vice-president-for-research |access-date=2026-05-10 |website=Texas A&M Stories |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Education and influences==
Wilson received her Bachelor of Science (BS) degree in chemistry from [[Eastern Washington University]] and her Ph.D. from the [[University of Minnesota]] in chemical physics. She was a [[Postdoctoral research|post-doctoral fellow]] at [[Pacific Northwest National Laboratory]] in the Environmental Molecular Sciences Laboratory (EMSL).  She worked on an MBA at the University of Oklahoma, and completed leadership training including the Harvard Institute for Management & Leadership in Education (MLE) program, Leadership America, Leadership Texas, and other programs. Some of her early influences were via the Girl Scouts,<ref>{{Cite web |title=A Science Career Rooted in Inspiration {{!}} Girl Scouts |url=https://www.girlscouts.org/en/our-stories/alumnae/dr-angela-wilson-science-career-inspiration.html |access-date=2023-02-01 |website=www.girlscouts.org}}</ref> where she earned a Gold Award, the highest award in Girl Scouts.

== Career ==

=== Academic and professional appointments ===
Wilson joined the Department of Chemistry at the [[University of North Texas]] in 2000 as an assistant professor. She became a full professor in 2009 and was named a Regents Professor in 2011. In 2005, she established and became the director of the Texas [[Center for Advanced Scientific Computing and Modeling]] (CASCaM).<ref>{{cite web |title=Thinking outside the beaker: research model saves time, money |url=http://web3.unt.edu/news/story.cfm?story=9369 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090924074042/http://web3.unt.edu/news/story.cfm?story=9369 |archive-date=24 September 2009 |access-date=23 July 2009}}</ref>

Following multiple roles within the Department of Chemistry and a two-year administrative fellowship in the Office of the Provost and Vice President for Academic Affairs, in 2015, Wilson became the Associate Vice Provost for Faculty and led the Office of Faculty Success at the university, working with ~2,400 faculty and ~58 department chairs.

In 2016, Wilson was recruited to the [[National Science Foundation|National Science Foundation (NSF)]], where she served in the senior executive service of the federal government as Director of the Division of Chemistry, heading the division from 2016 to 2018. There, she led the investments in chemistry research across the nation for NSF, with an annual  budget of ~$250M.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Widener |first=Andrea |title=NSF Names New Chemistry Chief {{!}} Chemical & Engineering News |url=http://cen.acs.org/articles/93/i37/NSF-Names-New-Chemistry-Chief.html?type=paidArticleContent |access-date=2016-03-20 |website=cen.acs.org}}</ref>

She also became John A. Hannah Distinguished Professor in 2016 at [[Michigan State University]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www2.chemistry.msu.edu/faculty/wilson/people/akwilson.htm|title=The Wilson Research Group: People|website=www2.chemistry.msu.edu|access-date=2016-03-20}}</ref> joining the Department of Chemistry. After her rotation at NSF, Wilson was an Academic Advancement Network Fellow in the Office of the Dean in the College of Agriculture and Natural Resources.<ref>{{Cite web|title=2018-19 Leadership Fellows Program  |url=https://ofasd.msu.edu/2018/11/06/2018-19-leadership-new-fellows-program/}}</ref> In 2019, she established and began to serve as director at the MSU Center for Quantum Computing, Science, and Engineering (MSU-Q).<ref>{{Cite web|title=MSU Center for Quantum Computing, Science, and Engineering | url=https://msuq.natsci.msu.edu/about/leadership.aspx}}</ref> At that time, she also helped to establish the MSU Center for PFAS Research.<ref>{{Cite web|title=MSU Center for PFAS Research |url=https://www.canr.msu.edu/pfas-research/}}</ref> In 2020, she became Associate Dean for Strategic Initiatives in the College of Natural Sciences. In 2024, she became Faculty Senate Chair at Michigan State University.  She was also named a University Distinguished Professor at MSU, and was recipient of the university's top faculty award - the William J. Beal Outstanding Faculty Award.

In 2026, she moved to Texas A&M University, where she is the Vice President for Research and the VPR Research Chair, with an appointment in the Department of Chemistry.  As the VPR, she leads the university's $1.4B research enterprise.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Read |first=5 Min |date=2025-12-17 |title=Texas A&M University names Dr. Angela Wilson as vice president for research |url=https://stories.tamu.edu/news/2025/12/17/texas-am-university-names-dr-angela-wilson-as-vice-president-for-research |access-date=2026-05-10 |website=Texas A&M Stories |language=en-US}}</ref>

==== Professional societies and activities ====
Wilson has held prominent leadership roles in major scientific societies. In 2022, she was president of the American Chemical Society (ACS), one of the world's largest scientific societies, with over 200,000 members and an annual operating budget of more than $700M, with two major business operations.  From 2021-2023, she served as a member of the ACS board of directors.  She has served on the Leadership Bureau of the International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry (IUPAC), as well as president of IUPAC Division I, the Division of Physical and Biophysical Chemistry.<ref>{{Cite web |title=IUPAC Division of Physical and Biophysical Chemistry |url=https://iupac.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/06/Division-I-Minutes-2017.pdf}}</ref>  She was chair of the chemistry section of the American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Angela Wilson elected chair-elect of AAAS chemistry section |url=https://msutoday.msu.edu/news/2019/angela-wilson-elected-chair-elect-of-aaas-chemistry-section}}</ref> For the U.S. National Academies, she served as the chair of the U.S. National Committee for IUPAC, and has served on the U.S. Delegation to the IUPAC General Assembly on five occasions, chairing the delegation twice.

In 2024, she was elected as Treasurer and member of the Board of Directors of the American Physical Society.<ref>{{Cite web |title=APS General Election Results |url=https://www.aps.org/about/governance/general-election}}</ref> She also serves on the Council and Council Executive Committee of the American Association for the Advancement of Science.<ref>{{cite web |title=AAAS Council Members |url=https://www.aaas.org/governance/council}}</ref>

=== Research ===
As a researcher, Wilson's work spans [[Physical chemistry|physical]], [[Theoretical chemistry|theoretical]], and [[computational chemistry]].  She is engaged in quantum mechanical and quantum dynamical method development, thermochemical and spectroscopic studies of small molecules, protein modeling and drug design, catalysis design, environmental challenges (i.e., CO<small>2</small>, [[Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances|PFAS]]), heavy element and transition metal chemistry, and mechanical properties of materials.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Angela K. Wilson |url=https://chemistry.natsci.msu.edu/faculty-research/faculty-members/wilson-angela.aspx |access-date=2023-02-01 |website=chemistry.natsci.msu.edu |language=en}}</ref>   Some of her computational chemistry methodologies, including ''ab initio'' correlation consistent basis sets, correlation consistent composite approach (ccCA), complete basis set (CBS) procedures, and multireference wavefunction diagnostics for transition metals are utilized worldwide.  Her recent work on PFAS has provided insight upon the impact of these species on human health and potential mitigation strategies in the environment, including soils.  For drug design, she has been engaged in the development of strategies for a variety of anti-inflammatory diseases, end-stage kidney function, tuberculosis, and pediatric blastoma.

=== Publications, Editorships, Conferences, and Board Service ===

=== Author ===
Wilson has published over 200 peer-reviewed articles in scientific journals.

=== Editor ===
Wilson is the editor of Annual Reports in Computational Chemistry.  She is on the editorial advisory board for ''[[Cell Reports Physical Science]]''. She has served as an editor of ''[[Computational and Theoretical Chemistry]]'', as a member of the editorial advisory boards for the ''[[Journal of Physical Chemistry]]'' and ''[[International Journal of Quantum Chemistry]]'', and as a member of the editorial board for ''[[Scientific Reports]]''

In 2018, she chaired the Gordon Conference on Computational Chemistry.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.grc.org/computational-chemistry-conference/2018/ |title=2018 Computational Chemistry Conference GRC }}</ref>

She has edited seven books, including ''Pioneers of Quantum Chemistry''.<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Thomas Strom |first1=E. |url=https://pubs.acs.org/isbn/9780841227163 |title=Pioneers of Quantum Chemistry |last2=Wilson |first2=Angela K. |date=2013 |isbn=978-0-8412-2716-3 |series=ACS Symposium Series |volume=1122 |doi=10.1021/bk-2013-1122}}</ref>

Wilson is a frequent speaker on national and global science policy, as well as on her research, success in science, leadership, and many other topics.  She has given over 500 invited talks, including named lectures - the Robert S. Mulliken lecture, the Karton-Barton lecture, the Charles A. Abbott lecture, the William A. Smart lecture, and the Charles Reed lecture.

She serves on the boards of quantum computing companies (non-profit and for-profit), as well multiple conferences.

Olin Medal]], 2015<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.acs.org/content/acs/en/funding-and-awards/awards/national/recipients/2015-national-award-recipients.html|title=2015 National Award Recipients|website=American Chemical Society|access-date=2016-03-20}}</ref>
* University of North Texas Eminent Scholar Award, 2015
* [[Michigan Women's Hall of Fame]],2018
* Outstanding Achievement Award, University of Minnesota, 2020 <ref>{{Cite web|url=https://cse.umn.edu/chem/news/alumna-angela-wilson-receives-outstanding-achievement-award |title=Alumna Angela Wilson receives Outstanding Achievement Award &#124; Department of Chemistry &#124; College of Science and Engineering }}</ref>
* MSU College of Natural Sciences (NatSci) Outstanding Faculty Award, Michigan State University, 2022 <ref>{{Cite web| url=https://natsci.msu.edu/news/2022-11-2022-annual-awards-ceremony-honors-natsci-faculty-staff-and-students.aspx | title=2022 annual awards ceremony honors NatSci faculty, staff and students }}</ref>
* William J. Beal Outstanding Faculty Award, Michigan State University, 2023 <ref>{{Cite web|title=Faculty and staff honored, celebrated at MSU Awards Convocation |url=https://msutoday.msu.edu/news/2023/faculty-and-staff-honored-celebrated-at-msu-awards-convocation}}</ref>
* [[Iota Sigma Pi]] National Honorary Member, 2023
* [[Association for Women in Science]] Zenith Award, 2023
She is a Fellow of the [[American Chemical Society]] (2010), [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] (2012), the [[American Physical Society]] (2013), and the Royal Society of Chemistry (2021).

Wilson was one of three women interviewed for Nature Computational Science 3, 810–812 (2023) "Celebrating Women in Science" in honor of Ada Lovelace Day.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Rastogi |first=Ananya |title=Tackling environmental challenges, one molecule at a time, Nature Computational Science 3, 810-812 (2023). |journal=Nature Computational Science |date=2023 |volume=3 |issue=10 |pages=810–812 |doi=10.1038/s43588-023-00537-9 |pmid=38177761 |url=https://doi.org/10.1038/s43588-023-00537-9 |url-access=subscription }}</ref>. In 2025, she was named a University Distinguished Professor at Michigan State University.
